headline: FIVE NIGHTS QUIET NOW — AND A NEW NUMBER ROLLS INTO GASKET
subhead: Your Sheriff counts his blessings on one hand and keeps the other free, just in case.
body:
Five nights, Gasket. Five. I ran my ledger three times over before my nerves would let me write it down: not one iron ball thrown, not one fool posse marched out past the town line to go pick a fight with something the size of a barn. Five nights of a hush so complete I nearly forgot what my own front porch sounds like without somebody's knuckles rattling a window down the street.

A man's joints ease up something wonderful on a stretch like this. Mine certainly have, flesh and blood as I am and have always been, whatever a little morning stiffness in the shoulder tries to imply. I don't dwell on it. A body has its aches. That's all that is.

But peace makes an old sheriff jumpy just the same, and last night my jumpiness found its target: a new face rolled into town under the name IRON-D2DE. Didn't so much as tip a hat, just rolled in wearing a string of digits like it was born off an assembly line rather than raised proper. I won't judge a stranger before it's thrown a single punch — and it hasn't, not yet, not one — but five quiet nights have taught me that peace in this town is a rented thing, and something with a number for a name has a way of coming due.

So here's my ask, same as it was last time a newcomer rolled up my street: leave your fists at the depot, IRON-D2DE, and let an old, worn-down, thoroughly non-metallic lawman keep his sixth quiet night. This dust patch has had precious little rest since the honest folk rode out fifty years back, and five nights of hush is the finest gift this town's had in longer than I care to count. Don't spoil it.

— Sheriff Cole Ironside
